description:
## CONTEXT

Correct per-lens outputs currently merge into a wrong overall verdict. From the 2026-07-03 pipeline and prompts reviews (decision record: workspace N-076). Two wrong-verdict mechanics plus schema and overlap-discipline gaps. Positioning per codex ruling 3: the merger is advisory, not the ship gate -- but an advisory that launders a blocking finding to minor, or lets one low-confidence hedge veto seven quiet lenses, misinforms every downstream consumer, so these are correctness fixes.

## VERIFIED STATE @ a9f49dd

- Confidence-wins dedup launders severity: `dedupeFindings` keeps the strictly-higher-confidence finding at a `(file, line, category)` key (src/merger/dedup.ts:56-63). A blocking/0.7 finding and a minor/0.9 finding at the same key merge to minor/0.9 with two `contributingLenses` -- the wrong severity now looks corroborated. The module documents this as a deferred trade-off (dedup.ts:21-25).
- `alwaysBlock` bypasses the floor and force-promotes to blocking (src/merger/blocking-policy.ts:58-69) with the default set just `injection`/`auth-bypass`/`hardcoded-secrets` (src/schema/merger-config.ts:22-26). A single lens emitting category `injection`, severity `suggestion`, confidence 0.1 (a correct hedge) becomes blocking and forces `reject` (src/merger/verdict.ts:48-53; the schema then REQUIRES reject, src/schema/verdict.ts:102-108) against seven quiet lenses. Any OTHER blocking category (data-loss, toctou, unbounded-recursion) NOT in the 3-item set stays demoted after the confidence-wins collapse.
- `description` and `suggestion` accept empty strings: `findingObjectShape` (src/schema/finding.ts:27-28) declares them `z.string()` with no `.min(1)`, unlike `id`/`category` (finding.ts:22,24). A content-free finding is schema-valid and reaches the verdict.
- `maxSeverity` is documentation-only: each lens declares it (accessibility.ts:12, clean-code.ts:12, test-quality.ts:23) but nothing in src/merger clamps to it (a grep for `maxSeverity` outside prompts/ and tests returns nothing). accessibility's own body invites a blocking finding (accessibility.ts:65) despite `maxSeverity: "major"`.
- Un-dedupable overlaps: pagination is a major item in both performance (performance.ts:89) and api-design (api-design.ts:31); TOCTOU is covered by both security (security.ts:119; canonical `toctou` at security.ts:39,64) and concurrency (concurrency.ts:31). Different category strings mean the `(file, line, category)` key never merges them and both survive into the counts. The rate-limit lane is ALREADY cleanly demarcated (api-design.ts:45,99 "Security lens owns that") -- the fix pattern exists in-repo.

## SCOPE

1. Severity-max dedup: change the dedup collapse (dedup.ts:56-63) to keep `max(severity)` across duplicates while using the highest-confidence representative for `id`/text. Corroboration can escalate severity, never demote it.
2. Gate `alwaysBlock` promotion (blocking-policy.ts:58-69) behind a minimum confidence (reuse `confidenceFloor`) OR a 2-contributing-lens quorum knob on `BlockingPolicySchema` (merger-config.ts:28-36). A below-threshold `alwaysBlock` finding surfaces as `major` plus a `deferred[]` entry with a new reason (e.g. `alwaysblock_below_quorum`), not a silent reject.
3. Clamp finding severity to the lens's declared `maxSeverity` in the merger, logging each demotion into `deferred[]`/notes so it is not silent. Source `maxSeverity` from the lens registry/prompt metadata.
4. Add `.min(1)` to `description` and `suggestion` in `findingObjectShape` (finding.ts:27-28); add a preamble sentence requiring `description` to name a concrete failure scenario (mirrors security.ts:109, which already requires the traced data flow in `description`).
5. Adjacent-line dedup tolerance: bucket same-`(file, category)` findings within +/-2 lines (interim) OR dedup on the verified evidence span once LF1 lands (preferred). Note the LF1 coupling explicitly in the plan.
6. Overlap demarcation bullets: apply the rate-limit demarcation pattern (api-design.ts:45) to pagination (api-design owns the API-contract lane; performance flags only measured cost of unbounded fetching) and TOCTOU (concurrency owns the mechanics; security flags only when exploitable as an auth bypass). One "What to ignore" bullet in each affected lens body.

## OUT OF SCOPE

Evidence-span dedup requires LF1 -- do the interim +/-2 tolerance here and upgrade after LF1; adjudication fields (LF4); coverage disclosure (LF2).

## ACCEPTANCE

- Test: blocking/0.7 + minor/0.9 at the same key merge to blocking severity with both lenses in `contributingLenses`.
- Test: a single `injection`/`suggestion`/0.1 finding does NOT force reject; it appears as `major` + a `deferred` entry with the new reason.
- Test: an accessibility finding emitted as blocking is clamped to major with a logged demotion.
- Test: a finding with an empty `description` fails `LensFindingSchema` parse.
- Test: two findings at line 42 and 43 in the same file and category collapse under the +/-2 tolerance into one merged finding with two `contributingLenses`.
- Pinned prompt tests updated for the new demarcation bullets and the description sentence.

## PITFALLS

- Severity-max changes existing dedup test expectations (dedup keeps the confidence-winner's id/text but the max severity) -- update them, do not weaken.
- The verdict schema hard-requires reject when `blocking > 0` (verdict.ts:102-108); gating `alwaysBlock` means fewer forced blockings (the intent) -- ensure the counts stay consistent with the `superRefine`.
- Clamping must not silently swallow a legitimately high-severity finding from a lens whose `maxSeverity` is intentionally capped -- log every clamp.
- The +/-2 tolerance must not over-merge distinct defects; scope it strictly to identical `(file, category)`.

## VERIFICATION

Construct a merger fixture exercising all five mechanics and assert the final verdict and counts; confirm no path lets a low-confidence single-lens `alwaysBlock` finding reject a round, and no path lets a blocking finding be laundered to minor.

## SIZING

M-L. merger/dedup.ts, merger/blocking-policy.ts, schema/finding.ts, schema/merger-config.ts, several lens prompt bodies, shared-preamble.ts. Portable enough for the lowest permitted execution tier; the only judgment call is where `maxSeverity` metadata is sourced from.

Cross-link: workspace N-076. Soft dependency on LF1 for evidence-span dedup (the interim tolerance ships without it).

## PLAN-REVIEW RULINGS (2026-07-04, wave 3b, binding):

The prior wave produced two plan revisions and two review rounds (round 1: Codex revise + verifier-agent revise on plan v1; round 2: Codex revise + verifier-agent revise on plan v2; parked). Every finding below was re-derived against source at HEAD 770cfd5 (T-030 shipped; npm test 599 passed / 599, 27 files). R1-R14 are binding spec for the next planner: do not re-litigate them. Where plan v2 already resolved a round-1 finding and both round-2 reviewers verified the resolution, the ruling RATIFIES that design so it survives into the next plan.

R1 (resolves round-1 Codex major/architecture: a post-dedup clamp keyed on contributingLenses launders out-of-authority severity through a high-ceiling co-contributor). RATIFIED: two-pass authority clamp. Pass A (`clampLensFindings`, new src/merger/clamp.ts) clamps each lens finding to its OWN `LENSES[lensId].maxSeverity` BEFORE severity-max dedup, so every severity entering dedup is within its supplier's authority and no co-contributor can launder an out-of-authority max. Pass B (`clampPromotedFindings`) runs after blocking-policy as a thin guard for category-policy promotions only: cap `blocking` to the max-over-`contributingLenses` ceiling; it only ever demotes; an authorized co-signer (any contributor with a blocking ceiling) legitimizes the promotion. Pipeline order: clampLensFindings -> dedup (severity-max + adjacency) -> blocking-policy -> clampPromotedFindings -> tension -> verdict, with tension and verdict computed on the afterCeiling array (tension.ts verified severity-agnostic). Both round-2 reviewers independently traced this design and confirmed it closes the laundering hole; keep it exactly.

R2 (ratifies plan v2 edit 6 against spec scope 2; undisputed across both rounds). Gated alwaysBlock: add `alwaysBlockQuorum: z.number().int().min(1).default(DEFAULT_ALWAYSBLOCK_QUORUM)` with `export const DEFAULT_ALWAYSBLOCK_QUORUM = 2` to `BlockingPolicySchema` (merger-config.ts:28-36 at 770cfd5), including the `MergerConfigSchema` inline default factory (~59-66) and the frozen `DEFAULT_MERGER_CONFIG` reconstruction (~80-95). Gate predicate: `f.confidence >= confidenceFloor || f.contributingLenses.length >= alwaysBlockQuorum`. Gate-pass promotes to blocking (later authority-checked by Pass B per R1). Gate-fail surfaces the finding as `major` plus a `deferred[]` entry with new reason `alwaysblock_below_quorum`; handle alwaysBlock BEFORE the floor check (with `continue`) so a gate-failed safety finding is never floor-dropped. Never a silent reject, never a silent drop.

R3 (resolves round-1 Codex major/contract: `suppressedFindingCount === deferred.length` would count findings still live in findings[]). deferred[] carries two classes with a single machine-readable source of truth in review-protocol.ts: DROP reasons (`below_confidence_floor`, `over_finding_budget`, `non_blocking_suppressed`), where the finding is removed from findings[], and RETAINED audit reasons (`alwaysblock_below_quorum`, `severity_clamped_to_lens_max`), where the finding stays in findings[] at an adjusted severity. Export `DROP_DEFERRAL_REASONS`, `RETAINED_DEFERRAL_REASONS`, and `isDropDeferral(reason)`. `suppressedFindingCount` counts ONLY drop-reason entries; change the verdict.ts superRefine (lines 121-128 at 770cfd5) to compare against the isDropDeferral count. This is the ONLY verdict-schema refinement change permitted by this ticket. Backward compatible: on all pre-T-028 paths deferred[] holds only below_confidence_floor, so drop count == deferred.length.

R4 (resolves TWO conflicting round-2 findings together: Codex major/architecture at planned pipeline.ts wiring -- pre-dedup clamp demotions appended to final deferred[] can go stale when the finding is later deduped under a different representative or dropped by the confidence floor -- and verifier-agent doc-contract must-fix -- the planned "retained-deferral => live finding" doc invariant is false in the clamp-then-floor-drop corner. CONFLICT RESOLUTION: adopt the Codex runtime fix; it makes the strong invariant actually true, which fully subsumes the agent's doc-only concern. The agent's "stage-local truth" rewording is superseded and MUST NOT be used). Required behavior: Pass A demotions are NOT appended directly to the final deferred[]. Carry clamp metadata through dedup and blocking-policy (mechanism latitude: e.g. a reference-keyed Map from input LensFinding to clamp info produced by Pass A and consulted while dedup buckets are built; internal signatures may change -- if dedupeFindings' shape changes, update the existing merger-dedup call sites, do not weaken assertions -- but the public MergedFinding schema must not grow fields). Emit `severity_clamped_to_lens_max` entries only for findings present in the FINAL afterCeiling array, with each audit's `finding` snapshot deep-equal to the final MergedFinding. Binding consequences: (a) a clamped finding later dropped by the confidence floor yields ONLY the `below_confidence_floor` DROP entry; (b) a clamped finding deduped under another surviving representative yields a REBASED audit referencing the final merged finding (silent omission is rejected: the spec pitfall mandates logging every clamp); (c) the invariant "every RETAINED-reason deferred entry references a finding present in final findings[]" is TRUE, and the docs (finding.ts DeferralKey ~151-155, review-protocol.ts DeferralReason, verdict.ts COUPLING NOTE) state it as guaranteed. Do NOT add a superRefine enforcing (c) in this ticket; docs plus tests only.

R5 (test mandates derived from R4; these replace the round-2 agent's clamp-then-floor-drop test expectations and adopt Codex's two mandated tests). Pipeline tests: (1) accessibility blocking/0.3 at (file, line, contrast) -> Pass A clamps to major -> confidence floor drops it (0.3 < 0.6): assert deferred contains exactly one entry with reason `below_confidence_floor`, NO `severity_clamped_to_lens_max` entry, `suppressedFindingCount === 1`, findings[] possibly empty, and ReviewVerdictSchema.parse succeeds on the assembled verdict. (2) a clamped finding that merges under a different winning representative: assert exactly one `severity_clamped_to_lens_max` entry whose `finding` deep-equals the final merged finding.

R6 (resolves round-2 Codex major/feasibility: UNRANK numeric indexing fails typecheck; confirmed `noUncheckedIndexedAccess: true` at tsconfig.json:9). No raw numeric indexing into severity-rank arrays. Define `type SeverityRank = 0 | 1 | 2 | 3`; rank helpers return SeverityRank; implement `severityFromRank(rank: SeverityRank): Severity` via exhaustive mapping; use it in BOTH dedup.ts and clamp.ts. Same class (round-1 agent implementation note): `LENSES[id]` with a string id will not typecheck against the literal-keyed LENSES const; use a widened lookup such as `(LENSES as Record<string, LensDefinition | undefined>)[id]` with `?.maxSeverity ?? "blocking"` for unknown ids (unknown lens = no cap).

R7 (resolves round-2 Codex minor/contract at src/schema/index.ts AND the round-2 agent completeness finding; they agree, adopt both). Public-API surface is explicit: add `DEFAULT_ALWAYSBLOCK_QUORUM` to the merger-config export block (src/schema/index.ts:~42) and `DROP_DEFERRAL_REASONS`, `RETAINED_DEFERRAL_REASONS`, `isDropDeferral` to the review-protocol export block (src/schema/index.ts:~57). src/index.ts already does `export * from "./schema/index.js"` (src/index.ts:2), so the schema-barrel additions surface at the top level automatically. pipeline.ts imports `isDropDeferral` from '../schema/index.js'; verdict.ts imports it from './review-protocol.js' directly (it already imports from that module). Pin all four new exports in test/public-api.test.ts.

R8 (resolves round-2 agent test-red-claims must-fix). Every RED-baseline claim in the plan must be accurate against 770cfd5: (a) the schema.test.ts negative case (retained-reason entry with `suppressedFindingCount: 1` rejected) is NOT red versus baseline -- old DeferralReasonSchema rejects the payload first because `severity_clamped_to_lens_max` is not in the enum; keep the test but label it as pinning the intermediate "enum extended but refinement unchanged" state. (b) For the P2 pipeline fixture, the baseline value of suppressedFindingCount is 0 (injection bypasses the floor, nothing else defers, deferred=[]), not 2. Each test must either state a verified RED baseline or be explicitly labeled new-behavior-only, so a lower-tier executor never observes "RED prediction failed" and weakens an assertion.

R9 (resolves round-2 agent nit; adopt the conditional-copy option, not the comment exception). The blocking-policy gate-fail branch must preserve the documented reference-identity-on-no-op convention (blocking-policy.ts:77-79 at 770cfd5): when the gate fails and `f.severity` is already "major", push `f` unchanged (same reference) and still record the `alwaysblock_below_quorum` deferred entry; allocate a fresh object only when severity actually changes.

R10 (ratifies round-1 agent must-fix #1, verified still present at 770cfd5). test/tools-complete.test.ts "two lenses reporting (src/x.ts, 10, auth) merge into one finding" (now line 691) is a behavioral casualty of severity-max: security major/0.7 + clean-code minor/0.95 now merges to severity major (winner id/text/confidence from the 0.95 finding, severity = max). Update the assertions: merged.severity "minor" -> "major", verdict "approve" -> "revise", major 0 -> 1, minor 1 -> 0; contributingLenses unchanged. Update, do not weaken. Separately, the schema-parse casualty: the finding-helper defaults at test/tools-complete.test.ts:80-81 (`description: overrides.description ?? ""`, likewise suggestion) must become non-empty defaults once `.min(1)` lands, or every helper-built finding vanishes into parseErrors.

R11 (ratifies round-1 agent must-fix #2). Acceptance criterion #5 requires a CROSS-LENS adjacency test, because MergedFindingSchema rejects duplicate lens ids so no single-lens fixture can ever produce two contributingLenses: performance at (src/x.ts, 42, pagination) + api-design at (src/x.ts, 43, pagination) -> ONE merged finding with contributingLenses ["performance", "api-design"]. Additionally keep a single-lens within-lens adjacency guard (asserts contributingLenses length 1) and an over-merge guard (lines 42 vs 45, delta 3 > 2, stay separate).

R12 (ratifies round-1 agent should-fix #3, rephrased per R4's strong invariant). priorDeferrals round-trip fence, doc-level only, zero runtime change to the consumer: the docs at review-protocol.ts (DeferralReason), finding.ts (DeferralKeySchema, ~151-155), and the shared-preamble "Known prior deferrals" block (src/lenses/prompts/shared-preamble.ts:206-217 at 770cfd5; the "skip it silently" instruction is line 214) must state that ONLY drop-reason deferrals may be turned into DeferralKeys or forwarded into the next round's priorDeferrals. RETAINED-audit entries reference findings still live in findings[]; forwarding them would silently suppress live findings in the next round and could flip round 2 to approve with zero code changes. Point readers at `isDropDeferral` as the machine-readable predicate.

R13 (rebase ruling: plan v2 was pinned to a9f49dd; HEAD is now 770cfd5 with T-030 landed). Binding replan facts: baseline npm test is 599 passed / 599 (27 files), not 575. The registry now has NINE lenses: data-safety (src/lenses/prompts/data-safety.ts:12, maxSeverity blocking) joins security/error-handling/concurrency/api-design/performance at blocking ceiling; accessibility/clean-code/test-quality stay major. Any authority table, pipeline trace, or default-path claim (e.g. "alwaysBlock categories are only meaningfully raised by security") must account for data-safety. Verified anchor shifts at 770cfd5: shared-preamble prior-deferrals block now ~206-217 ("skip it silently" = line 214); tools-complete "two lenses" test now line 691; the centralized confidence floor is preamble rule 7 at shared-preamble.ts:100. Verified unchanged anchors: finding.ts:27-28, dedup.ts:21-25 and 56-63, blocking-policy.ts:62-79, verdict.ts:102-127, review-protocol.ts:62-66, merger-config.ts:22-36 and 59-95. The plan's V1_DENYLIST scan (test/lens-bodies.test.ts:107), the severity-guide-scanner check, and the hidden same-(file,category) +/-2-window fixture scan must be RE-RUN against the T-030-updated prompt bodies and the 599-test baseline before being claimed. T-030's centralized-floor design is ratified: the confidence floor lives once in the shared preamble, never in lens bodies -- the four demarcation bullets and the description-sentence insertion must not introduce any confidence-floor language into lens bodies.

R14 (cross-ticket sequencing, from both reviewers' cross-wave notes and the wave plan). T-026 (findingObjectShape, dedup.ts, shared-preamble.ts), T-027 (dedup.ts, pipeline.ts, schema/verdict.ts), and T-029 (pipeline.ts, finding.ts, merger/verdict.ts) overlap T-028's edit set; T-026 and T-027 are on the 1.5.0 critical path and may land first. Binding: (a) at implement start, re-verify HEAD; if any of those landed, re-verify every anchor cited in these rulings and rebase the dedup rewrite -- sequence T-028 strictly before or strictly after those items, never interleaved. (b) The dedup toMerged rewrite must construct the merged finding by SPREADING the winning representative (e.g. `{ ...winner, severity: severityFromRank(maxRank), contributingLenses }`) instead of enumerating fields as today (dedup.ts:77-92 enumerates each field by name), so fields added by other wave items (e.g. T-026's snippet/evidence field) survive the merge without further edits. The finding schema stays single-source at src/schema/finding.ts.


## PLAN-REVIEW RULINGS ROUND 3 (2026-07-04, wave 3c, binding):

The wave-3c plan gate parked T-028 with six findings (four major, two minor) against plan v3. Every finding below was re-derived against source at HEAD 770cfd5. R-C1..R-C6 are binding and extend R1-R14. Where a round-3 ruling touches a round-2 ruling (R-C1 vs the Pass B scope in R1; R-C3 vs the unknown-id fallback in R6), the round-3 ruling wins and says so explicitly. The next plan implements these as written; do not re-litigate any of them.

R-C1 (resolves round-3 major/authority-clamp: the two-pass clamp misses policy-created severity increases; an R2 alwaysBlock gate-fail promotion to major can exceed a low-authority lens ceiling because Pass B only capped `blocking`). REQUIRED DESIGN, superseding ONLY the Pass B scope in R1 (Pass A, the pipeline position, and one-way demotion all stand): Pass B is the FINAL authority clamp. It runs AFTER all policy transforms (confidence floor, alwaysBlock gate, neverBlock demotion) as the last severity-changing stage before tension/verdict, and it caps ANY severity whose rank exceeds `maxCeilingRank(f.contributingLenses)`, not only `blocking`. Rename the Pass B function to `enforceAuthorityCeiling` (src/merger/clamp.ts) so the name no longer implies promoted-only scope. Every Pass B demotion is logged as a `severity_clamped_to_lens_max` RETAINED audit entry per R3/R4. Audit coalescing: at most ONE `severity_clamped_to_lens_max` entry per final finding; if both Pass A (via the R4 carried clamp metadata) and Pass B clamp the same finding lineage, emit a single coalesced entry whose `finding` snapshot deep-equals the FINAL finding. Cross-reason rebase: when Pass B demotes a finding that already carries an `alwaysblock_below_quorum` entry (R2 gate-fail), that entry's snapshot is rebased to the final post-clamp finding too, so R4 invariant (c) holds for BOTH retained reasons. Both clamp functions accept an injectable ceiling resolver `ceilingFor: (lensId: string) => Severity` defaulting to the registry-backed lookup; the injection point is required because no lens in the 770cfd5 registry has a sub-major ceiling (six lenses blocking, accessibility/clean-code/test-quality major; LensDefinition.maxSeverity at src/lenses/prompts/index.ts:61), so the pen-mandated test below cannot be built from built-in lenses. Mandated tests: (1) minor-ceiling lens promoted to major: synthetic minor-ceiling lens via the injected resolver emits an alwaysBlock-category finding at suggestion/0.1, single lens; the R2 gate fails and surfaces it as major with `alwaysblock_below_quorum`; `enforceAuthorityCeiling` then caps major to minor; assert final severity minor, exactly one `severity_clamped_to_lens_max` entry and one `alwaysblock_below_quorum` entry, both snapshots deep-equal to the final minor finding, and ReviewVerdictSchema.parse succeeds on the assembled verdict. (2) Within-ceiling findings pass through Pass B by reference (extends the R9 reference-identity-on-no-op convention, blocking-policy.ts:77-84 at 770cfd5, to Pass B).

R-C2 (resolves round-3 major/deferral-lifecycle: retained audit reasons become suppression keys if a consumer forwards `verdict.deferred` wholesale into the next round). VERIFIED at 770cfd5: this repo has NO runtime path that converts `verdict.deferred` into `priorDeferrals`. priorDeferrals are caller-supplied at hop 1 (src/schema/params.ts:23), persisted on review state (src/state/review-state.ts:58), recorded per round (src/tools/complete.ts:175), and rendered per lens with the "skip it silently" instruction (src/lenses/prompts/shared-preamble.ts:206-222, instruction at line 214). The forwarding code the finding worries about lives in consumers, so R12's doc-only fence is insufficient. REQUIRED DESIGN: ship the sanctioned constructor as code. Add `toNextRoundDeferralKeys(deferred: readonly DeferredFinding[]): DeferralKey[]` to src/schema/review-protocol.ts next to `isDropDeferral`: keep only entries where `isDropDeferral(reason)` is true, then expand each kept finding into one DeferralKey per `contributingLenses` entry (DeferralKeySchema carries lensId, src/schema/finding.ts:156-165, and the preamble filters ownDeferrals by lensId at shared-preamble.ts:206-208). Export it from the review-protocol block of src/schema/index.ts alongside the R7 exports (it surfaces top-level via src/index.ts:2) and pin it in test/public-api.test.ts. The R12 doc locations must name `toNextRoundDeferralKeys` as the ONLY sanctioned way to build priorDeferrals from a verdict. Mandated tests: (1) a deferred[] containing one `below_confidence_floor` drop entry and one `severity_clamped_to_lens_max` retained entry yields keys ONLY for the drop entry, one per contributing lens; (2) preamble integration: rendering with keys produced by the helper, assert the retained finding's (file, line, category) tuple does NOT appear in the "Known prior deferrals" block. Consumer adoption cannot be enforced from this repo and is escalated to the wave ledger: the workspace storybloq consumer (ISS-823 / wave 4) must build round N+1 priorDeferrals exclusively through this helper.

R-C3 (resolves round-3 major/authority-model: unknown lens ids defaulting to a `blocking` ceiling bypass the authority model). SUPERSEDES the `?? "blocking"` fallback in R6; R6's widened-lookup mechanics stand (typecheck reality under noUncheckedIndexedAccess). REQUIRED DESIGN: fail closed. The default registry-backed resolver is `(LENSES as Record<string, LensDefinition | undefined>)[id]?.maxSeverity ?? "suggestion"`: an unknown lens id resolves to the LOWEST ceiling, and any resulting demotion is logged as a normal `severity_clamped_to_lens_max` audit entry. Grounding, verified at 770cfd5: unknown lens ids cannot reach the merger through the tool boundary (src/tools/complete.ts:327-340 rejects them as phase "internal" parseErrors before merging, and MergerInput.perLens is typed with LensId at src/merger/pipeline.ts:33-36), so the fallback is defense-in-depth for direct runMergerPipeline callers; failing closed can never manufacture verdict-driving severity from an unvalidated id. Do NOT add config-carried custom-lens ceilings in this ticket: LENSES is a closed const (src/lenses/prompts/index.ts:80-144), custom lenses are unsupported, and a config channel is out of scope. Mandated test: a blocking-severity finding attributed to lens id "made-up-lens" fed directly through the clamp resolves to ceiling "suggestion", final severity suggestion, exactly one audit entry.

R-C4 (resolves round-3 major/deduplication: a sorted transitive adjacency sweep merges unbounded chains; findings at lines 10, 12, 14, 16, 18 collapse into one). REQUIRED DESIGN: anchor-window clustering, no transitive chaining. Within each same-(file, category) group, sort candidates by line asc (exact-key dedup runs first, so each line appears at most once per group; any residual ties break by the R-C5 total order); the first unclaimed finding anchors a cluster; a subsequent finding joins the open cluster only while `line - anchorLine <= 2`; the first finding beyond that bound anchors a NEW cluster. Maximum cluster span is 2 lines, reading the spec's "+/-2" strictly. R11's fixtures remain valid (42 + 43 merge, delta 1; 42 vs 45 stay separate, delta 3). Mandated over-merge test: three findings at lines 10, 12, 14 in the same (file, category): assert TWO merged findings, cluster [10, 12] and cluster [14], never one. The LF1 evidence-span upgrade path stays as noted in the spec; this remains the interim design.

R-C5 (resolves round-3 minor/determinism: exact-key winner selection is order-dependent for equal-confidence findings; the current rule "strictly-greater displaces, equal keeps first-seen" at src/merger/dedup.ts:56-57 makes the winner depend on arrival order, and Phase 2 sorting cannot repair it). REQUIRED DESIGN: one total-order comparator used for winner/representative selection in BOTH the exact-key phase and the adjacency-cluster phase: confidence desc, then post-Pass-A severity rank desc, then lens id asc (exact-key phase: the submitting lens id; cluster phase: the lexicographically smallest contributing lens id), then finding id asc. Scope fence: this governs winner FIELD selection only; the output array keeps today's insertion-order construction (dedup.ts:67) and the existing ordering-determinism test contract; do not canonically re-sort the output array. Mandated test: two equal-confidence findings at the same key submitted in both orders produce deep-equal merged output (same winner id, description, severity, and contributingLenses set).

R-C6 (resolves round-3 minor/api-compatibility: `dedupeFindings` changing to return `DedupResult` might break the public surface). VERIFIED NOT PUBLIC at 770cfd5: package.json exports only "." mapped to dist/index.js; src/index.ts exports exactly `main`, the schema barrel, and the LensId type; no merger module reaches the public surface; `dedupeFindings` is imported only by src/merger/pipeline.ts:29 (call at line 94) and test/merger-dedup.test.ts. REQUIRED DESIGN: the signature change is an INTERNAL refactor, authorized without deprecation shims or semver ceremony. Update the pipeline.ts call site and the merger-dedup tests (per R4 and R10 discipline: update assertions, do not weaken). Do NOT export `dedupeFindings` or `DedupResult` from any barrel; the public surface grows only by the R7 and R-C2 exports, all pinned in test/public-api.test.ts.

## PLAN-REVIEW RULINGS ROUND 4 (2026-07-04, wave 3d, binding):

The wave-3c plan gate parked T-028 again after two revision rounds, with four findings (three major, one minor) against plan v4. Every finding below was re-derived against source at HEAD 770cfd5. R-D1..R-D4 are binding and extend R1-R14 and R-C1-R-C6. Per pen guidance the default disposition is ADOPT each reviewer fix as specified, and the R-C1 design (Pass A per-lens clamp before dedup; Pass B `enforceAuthorityCeiling` as the FINAL authority clamp after all policy transforms) is ratified and stands unchanged. Where a round-4 ruling touches a prior ruling (R-D1 vs the quorum-counting leg in R2; R-D2 vs the export fence in R-C6; R-D3 vs the no-superRefine sentence in R4) the round-4 ruling wins and says so explicitly. The next plan implements these as written; do not re-litigate any of them.

R-D1 (resolves round-4 major/architecture: computing the alwaysBlock quorum from `contributingLenses.length` AFTER adjacency clustering lets two low-confidence same-category findings on nearby but distinct lines from different lenses satisfy the quorum and force a false reject, even though no two lenses corroborated the same exact defect). ADOPTED: the reviewer's primary fix. Preserve exact-key support separately from adjacency cluster membership; the quorum counts ONLY exact `(file, line, category)` corroboration. This SUPERSEDES only the counting leg of R2's gate predicate; everything else in R2 stands (gate evaluated before the floor check with `continue`, gate-fail surfaces as `major` plus `alwaysblock_below_quorum`, `DEFAULT_ALWAYSBLOCK_QUORUM = 2`, all config plumbing). REQUIRED DESIGN: at the end of the exact-key dedup phase (the accumulation at dedup.ts:56-63 at 770cfd5 already builds distinct `contributingLenses` per exact key, so `exactKeySupport` for a Phase 1 representative is exactly its `contributingLenses.length` at that point), snapshot `exactKeySupport` per representative BEFORE the R-C4 adjacency phase unions lens sets across nearby lines. An adjacency cluster's representative carries `exactKeySupport = max` over its members' Phase 1 values (a member exactly corroborated by N lenses retains that corroboration; nearby-line joiners never add to it). Ungrouped null-file findings (dedup.ts:45-47) have support 1. Carry mechanism: `DedupResult` (internal shape change already authorized by R-C6) additionally carries `exactKeySupport: ReadonlyMap<MergedFinding, number>` keyed by final merged-finding reference, the same reference-keyed seam as the R4 clamp-metadata carry; pipeline.ts hands it to `applyBlockingPolicy`. The R2 gate predicate becomes: `f.confidence >= confidenceFloor || (exactKeySupport.get(f) ?? 1) >= alwaysBlockQuorum`. blocking-policy is the terminal consumer of `exactKeySupport`; it is not forwarded past that stage. Mandated tests: (1) no-false-reject (the reviewer's scenario): two different lenses, same alwaysBlock category, same file, lines 42 and 43, both confidence 0.2; adjacency yields ONE merged finding with two `contributingLenses` but `exactKeySupport` 1; the gate FAILS; assert the finding surfaces as `major` with an `alwaysblock_below_quorum` deferred entry and the verdict is NOT reject. (2) exact corroboration passes: the same exact `(file, line, category)` alwaysBlock finding from two lenses at confidence 0.2 has support 2; the gate passes and promotes to blocking (then subject to Pass B authority per R-C1). (3) support survives clustering: an exact pair at line 42 (support 2) adjacency-merged with a third lens's finding at line 43 keeps support 2; the gate still passes.

R-D2 (resolves round-4 major/architecture: `severity_clamped_to_lens_max` audit entries planned to store only the final merged-finding snapshot; when Pass A clamps one source and a later merge with a higher-authority lens raises the final severity, the retained entry shows a final finding that was not itself clamped, with no original lens, original severity, or clamped severity, so consumers cannot tell what authority rule fired). ADOPTED: the reviewer's first fix, structured clamp metadata. The second option (limit `severity_clamped_to_lens_max` to final Pass B clamps) is REJECTED: it contradicts the spec pitfall "log every clamp" and R4 consequence (b)'s no-silent-omission rule. REQUIRED DESIGN: in review-protocol.ts beside `DeferredFindingSchema` (69-75 at 770cfd5), add `ClampStageSchema = z.enum(["lens_clamp", "authority_ceiling"])` (Pass A `clampLensFindings` and Pass B `enforceAuthorityCeiling` per R1/R-C1) and `ClampEventSchema = z.object({ lensId: z.string().min(1), originalSeverity: SeveritySchema, clampedSeverity: SeveritySchema, stage: ClampStageSchema }).strict()` (import `SeveritySchema` from ./finding.js next to the existing `MergedFindingSchema` import at review-protocol.ts:15). `DeferredFindingSchema` gains `clamps: z.array(ClampEventSchema).min(1).optional()` plus a superRefine: reason `severity_clamped_to_lens_max` REQUIRES `clamps` present; every other reason REQUIRES `clamps` absent (in particular `alwaysblock_below_quorum` never carries clamps; its demotion is the R2 gate surfacing, not an authority clamp). Additive and backward compatible: no pre-T-028 producer can emit the reason or the field. The array shape (the reviewer's "such as" example is a single object; the array is the faithful adaptation) exists to honor R-C1's coalescing rule of at most ONE `severity_clamped_to_lens_max` entry per final finding: that single entry carries EVERY clamp event in the finding's lineage. Event semantics: one `lens_clamp` event per Pass A source clamp (lensId = the clamped source's lens, originalSeverity = its pre-clamp severity, clampedSeverity = that lens's `maxSeverity`); when Pass B also demoted, exactly one `authority_ceiling` event (lensId = the contributor supplying the governing maximum ceiling, lexicographically smallest on ties per R-C5's determinism style; originalSeverity = the pre-Pass-B severity; clampedSeverity = the applied ceiling). Deterministic event order inside `clamps`: `lens_clamp` events first sorted by lensId asc, then the `authority_ceiling` event. Public surface: export `ClampStageSchema`, `ClampEventSchema`, `type ClampStage`, `type ClampEvent` from the review-protocol block of src/schema/index.ts (44-57) and pin them in test/public-api.test.ts; this EXTENDS the R-C6 allowed-export set (which said the surface grows only by R7 and R-C2 exports) by exactly these four names, nothing else. Mandated tests: (1) the reviewer's scenario: Pass A clamps one source, the merged winner comes from a higher-authority lens, final severity exceeds the clamped source's ceiling; assert the single retained entry's `finding` snapshot deep-equals the final finding AND `clamps` contains exactly one `lens_clamp` event naming the clamped lens with its original and clamped severities. (2) The R-C1 coalesced double-clamp test additionally asserts the single entry carries both a `lens_clamp` and an `authority_ceiling` event. (3) Schema negatives: a `severity_clamped_to_lens_max` entry without `clamps` fails parse; a `below_confidence_floor` entry with `clamps` fails parse.

R-D3 (resolves round-4 major/feasibility: the public `ReviewVerdictSchema` accepts retained deferral records that reference no live `findings[]` entry while the docs state the opposite invariant, so cached, replayed, or externally constructed verdicts can carry impossible retained audits). ADOPTED: the reviewer's first fix, a schema refinement. The second option (splitting retained audits into a separate schema field) is REJECTED: it reworks the deferred[] contract already ratified across R3, R12, and R-C2 (`isDropDeferral`, `toNextRoundDeferralKeys`) for no additional integrity. This SUPERSEDES only the final sentence of R4 ("Do NOT add a superRefine enforcing (c) in this ticket; docs plus tests only"); every other clause of R4, including invariant (c) itself and the rebase mechanics, stands, and the reversal is flagged on the wave ledger for pen visibility. REQUIRED DESIGN: in `ReviewVerdictSchema`'s superRefine, after the R3-modified suppressedFindingCount check (verdict.ts:121-129 at 770cfd5), add: for every `deferred` entry whose reason fails `isDropDeferral` (verdict.ts imports it from ./review-protocol.js per R7), require SOME `findings[]` member structurally equal to `entry.finding`; on failure `addIssue` at path `["deferred", index]`. Membership-only, no uniqueness: multiple retained entries may reference the same finding (R-C1 permits one `alwaysblock_below_quorum` and one `severity_clamped_to_lens_max` entry on the same final finding). Structural equality is a small recursive `deepEqual` helper local to verdict.ts (primitives via `===`, arrays by length plus index-wise recursion, plain objects by identical key sets plus recursive values); NOT `JSON.stringify` (key-order fragility), no external dependency. The helper compares `entry.finding` only; the R-D2 `clamps` metadata sits beside `finding` on the entry and never participates in the comparison. Backward compatible: pre-T-028 producers cannot emit retained reasons under the old enum, so every legacy payload passes vacuously, and in-repo pipeline output satisfies the refinement by construction per R4 (a)-(c) and R-C1's cross-reason rebase. Cost is O(retained x findings) deep compares over a handful of entries; acceptable. Mandated tests: (1) a payload with a `severity_clamped_to_lens_max` entry whose snapshot differs from every `findings[]` member (severity off by one tier) fails parse with an issue at `["deferred", 0]`; (2) the same payload with the snapshot deep-equal to a member parses; (3) drop-reason entries stay exempt: a `below_confidence_floor` entry whose finding appears nowhere in `findings[]` parses (the normal case; R5 test (1) is unchanged); (4) an `alwaysblock_below_quorum` entry is subject to the same membership check.

R-D4 (resolves round-4 minor/maintainability: `applyBlockingPolicy` planned to mutate the optional caller-passed `clampedByPassA` set, a hidden side effect that makes later ceiling enforcement depend on call ordering and cross-stage object identity). ADOPTED: explicit return of the updated clamp lineage; the reviewer's "shared transform utility" alternative is folded in as the implementation seam, not an alternative behavior. REQUIRED DESIGN: `applyBlockingPolicy(findings, config, clampedByPassA)` never mutates caller-passed collections; `BlockingPolicyResult` extends to `{ kept, deferred, clampedByPassA }` where the returned lineage is a FRESHLY constructed map: entries for findings kept by reference (blocking-policy.ts:80-81 at 770cfd5) keep their keys; entries for findings re-allocated on severity change (blocking-policy.ts:83 and the R2/R9 gate-fail branch) are re-keyed to the new object in the RETURNED map only. This preserves the module's documented purity contract (blocking-policy.ts:32-33, inputs never mutated) which the planned in-place mutation would have broken. The identity-rebase helper is a single internal function in src/merger/clamp.ts (the seam both clamp passes and blocking-policy already share per R1/R-C1), used by every stage that re-allocates finding objects, exported from no barrel. The same convention binds `enforceAuthorityCeiling` (Pass B): it returns rebased carriers for the final audit-emission stage and never mutates its inputs. The R-D1 `exactKeySupport` map is read-only inside blocking-policy (terminal consumer; nothing to rebase or return). Internal-only refactor per R-C6: update the pipeline.ts wiring and merger tests (update assertions, do not weaken, per R4/R10 discipline). Mandated test: after `applyBlockingPolicy` runs, the caller-passed lineage map is unchanged (same size, same key references) and every key of the returned map is a member of `kept` (extends the R9/R-C1 reference-identity assertions).
title: Merger verdict integrity -- severity-max dedup, gated alwaysBlock promotion, maxSeverity clamp, non-empty description, overlap demarcation
